title: Tesla's Cybercab had a rocky first month in Austin. Now comes the hard part: expanding
source_used: Startup Fortune (citing Reuters, NHTSA, TechCrunch, Axios) and finance.biggo.com (citing Texas DMV records, Electrek); CNBC original blocked (403)
key_facts: Tesla's Cybercab, a two-seat robotaxi with no steering wheel, pedals or mirrors, began paid public rides in Austin on 3 Sep 2026.

NHTSA opened an audit query (AQ26002) the next morning into how Tesla self-certified the vehicle against federal safety standards written for cars with a driver; it covers roughly 1,000 vehicles (Startup Fortune, citing NHTSA).
Texas state records showed 420 Tesla autonomous vehicles registered at launch, of which 45 were Cybercabs (Startup Fortune citing Reuters; finance.biggo.com citing Texas DMV).
By early October Cybercab authorizations in Texas had risen to 169, with about 589 Tesla autonomous vehicles in all, against Waymo's fleet of more than 4,000 (finance.biggo.com).
Early passengers reported wait times above 45 minutes, wrong pickup points and occasional door and trunk malfunctions (finance.biggo.com).

Axios counted 10 incidents or complaints involving Tesla autonomous vehicles in Austin since testing began in June 2025, including failing to yield at a crosswalk and driving the wrong way (per Startup Fortune).
Austin fire officials warned that a Cybercab cannot be driven out of the way by first responders; Tesla's materials tell crews to call Robotaxi Support.
quote_evidence: Tesla launched commercial Cybercab rides in Austin, Texas on September 3, and the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration announced an audit query the next morning. NHTSA's probe is filed as AQ26002.

Public records from the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles show that on Cybercab's launch day, Tesla had 420 autonomous vehicles authorized for commercial operation in Texas—only 45 of which were Cybercabs
Multiple paying passengers reported on social media that wait times initially exceeded 45 minutes
why_it_matters_hint: Tesla's purpose-built robotaxi is real but tiny and under federal audit, and growing it city by city is the hard part.
